tickets.title: Pilot closing Third Avenue L stop
tickets.summary: Joshua Walk, a software engineer, presented a simulation based on 700 million MTA trips. It indicated that closing the Third Avenue L stop would save riders about 1,800 hours a day. He asked that the idea go to the transportation committee and that the board pilot the closure with the MTA. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and consider raising a pilot with the MTA.

tickets.title: 11th Street e-bike storage and delivery worker hub
tickets.summary: Over 100 e-bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on the block around the clock. This blocks the street and sidewalk and creates garbage and fire concerns, and businesses and tenants have left. The 9th Precinct plans an enforcement and bike confiscation action on October 7th. Groups asked for tagging for two weeks instead, and the signs are English only, so multilingual and verbal outreach is needed. The district manager has worked on this since February 2024 and a fenced site is being sought. Action: District office to keep working with the 9th Precinct, elected officials and worker groups on outreach, notice and a site for bike storage, and to follow the October 7th action.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark areas in Seward Park
tickets.summary: Many speakers and callers report more drug use and homelessness in Seward Park. The Seward Park Conservancy and the Lower East Side Ecology Center also complained, and needle collection is up in Tompkins Square Park as police presence displaces activity. A member noted dark spots in the park and asked about mobile crisis teams as an alternative to policing. Action: District office to follow up with the precinct, Parks and DOT, collect reports of lights that are out, and look at non-police options such as outreach and mobile crisis teams.

tickets.title: Indoor roller skating rink on East River pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: Analdi Diaz proposed a 300,000 square foot, three-story multi-use building on an East River pier. It would include an indoor roller skating rink with $8 admission and would create 250 to 500 jobs. She cited the closure of the city's historic rinks. Action: Refer the proposal to the land use committee for review.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP resolutions and postponement
tickets.summary: The joint land use and economic development committee met with EDC about the Essex Market RFP, which was due out at the end of the month. EDC could not say what from the board's two resolutions was incorporated. The board asked EDC to postpone issuing the RFP. Action: Land use chair, the district manager and EDC to meet later this week to clarify the resolutions, then report back to the board.

tickets.title: City housing plan comments and ongoing land use input
tickets.summary: The board commented on the city's draft housing plan using its district needs statement because of the short turnaround. The plan has about 7,000 units over five years, 75% of them market rate, and the board's top comment was that affordable housing is its highest need. Members asked about ongoing land use committee input, and the district manager said committees must take positions proactively. Action: Land use committee to take proactive positions on housing plans as notice periods shrink.

tickets.title: NYCHA, communication access and basic needs concerns
tickets.summary: Vincent Jenkins, who is hard of hearing, raised NYCHA housing struggles, lack of food, water and necessities, and the need for communication access for deaf people. He also asked for help with work and with drugs and toxicity in the community. Action: District office to follow up with the speaker on his NYCHA and communication access concerns.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot sites and resolution
tickets.summary: Two free pilot public restrooms are coming to the district, at Delancey and Suffolk and at Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue. DOT leads, installation is set for mid-October for a one-year pilot, and a private company keeps them clean. The committee has concerns about access and emergency calls, and the mayor's office asked for suggestions for tap-card partner locations. Action: Transportation committee to bring a resolution next month on access and next steps during the pilot.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge safety and Canal Street redesign update
tickets.summary: The board sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating its concerns at the exits of the Manhattan Bridge, citing a recent crash that killed a community member. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign project, on which there has been no update since January. Action: Follow up with DOT on the Canal Street redesign update and the Manhattan Bridge concerns.

tickets.title: Transportation equity analysis: crosstown buses and parking
tickets.summary: Board staff and the committee met with the Independent Budget Office to study whether CB3 gets its fair share of transportation. The ideas were narrowed to three, including crosstown buses and neighborhood parking locations. Action: Committee to pursue IBO research on crosstown buses and neighborhood parking and identify the third topic.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact report on FDR
tickets.summary: A member asked whether MTA or DOT will return to report on congestion pricing, noting that the board's earlier resolution flagged possible increased congestion on the FDR. The transportation committee chair said this was not on the committee's list but could be followed up. Action: Transportation committee to follow up and request reporting from MTA or DOT on congestion pricing impacts.

tickets.title: Correct SLA resolutions for Cozy Cafe, Softours Tea House
tickets.summary: August SLA items number 10 (Softours Tea House) and number 3 (Cozy Cafe) were for beer and wine licenses but the resolutions said full on-premises license. The committee chair acknowledged the clerical error and read the corrected wording to the board. Action: Correct both August resolutions to recommend denial of a beer and wine license unless stipulations are agreed to.

tickets.title: Allen Grill SLA denial and SLA follow-up
tickets.summary: The board passed a straight denial of the full liquor license for Allen Grill, from the operator of Time Cafe, by 20 yes, 10 no and 9 abstentions. The committee had earlier voted 3 to 2 for stipulations, so the denial leaves the board without enforceable stipulations if the SLA approves the license. Members were urged to attend the SLA hearing. Action: District office to add context to the resolution, watch the SLA calendar, and organize community members and elected official support to oppose the license at the SLA.

tickets.title: Mobile voting pilot for education council elections
tickets.summary: The Health and Human Services committee brought a resolution urging NYC public schools to pilot a mobile voting option for community and citywide education council elections, where turnout is about 2%. Members asked that outreach be multilingual, address immigrant families' fears, and make clear it is for school participation only. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the Department of Education with the outreach and clarity concerns noted.

tickets.title: Bylaw changes to attendance procedures
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would give members with too many absences in six months a letter and a meeting with the executive committee. Removal for attendance would be handled separately, and public members would be bound by the conflict of interest policies. A member noted a double recommendation in the draft wording. Action: Email the proposed changes to all members to meet the 28-day notice and vote on them at the October full board.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA and Robert's Rules
tickets.summary: The chair announced trainings on SLA matters, Robert's Rules and office procedures for new and existing members. Dates and times are not yet set, and members may email the chair with training topics or questions. Action: Schedule the trainings and announce dates, and collect training requests by email.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election
tickets.summary: The board held an election for second vice chair, with speeches by candidates Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas. Results were announced as Zachary Thomas 14 and Daniel Tano 25. Action: Daniel Tano is elected second vice chair; no further follow-up is needed.

tickets.title: Assign mentor to newest board member
tickets.summary: The chair welcomed newest board member Leila Mahia and said a mentor will be assigned to her in the near future. Action: Assign a mentor to the new member.

tickets.title: District needs and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: In October the board will vote on its district needs statement and expense and capital budget priorities, ranked by agency, in every committee except SLA. The priorities are based on committee work and meetings with over 20 agencies, and focus on programs needing funding, such as summer youth employment. Action: Committees to discuss and prepare ranked expense and capital priorities for the October vote.

tickets.title: East River Park construction delay and stewardship facility
tickets.summary: Part of the East River Park construction is delayed, specifically the new facility for the Lower East Side Ecology Center and stewardship programs, because of procurement challenges. The ESCR/BMCR team gave few details and will return in October. Community requests for better interim park stewardship support are to be addressed. Action: Parks committee to get the team's October update on the procurement delays and interim stewardship support.
